title: Sound Waves and Their Properties
text: Sound is a mechanical wave that travels through a medium (such as air, water, or solids) via vibrations of particles. Key properties include frequency (pitch, measured in Hertz), amplitude (loudness), and wavelength. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum because it requires a medium. The speed of sound in air at room temperature is about 343 meters per second, faster in water and faster still in solids. Human hearing typically ranges from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
